coredata.dc:description: Bisphenols are a group of industrial chemicals widely used in the manufacture of plastics and epoxy resins. Bisphenol F (BPF) is increasingly being used as a substitute for bisphenol A (BPA), which is a widely used environmental endocrine-disrupting chemical (EDC) and hypothesized obesogen. Nevertheless, limited research has examined the potential of BPF to induce obesity, leaving a knowledge gap. To address this issue, this study investigated the effect of BPF on the differentiation of 3T3-L1 preadipocyte and its underlying mechanisms. 3T3-L1 preadipocytes were cultured and induced to differentiate in controlled conditions, then exposed to varying BPF doses over an 8-day period. Significant increases in intracellular lipid droplets and triglyceride (TG) content were observed in the treated cells, indicating that BPF has a stimulating effect on adipogenesis. In BPF-treated 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, key adipogenic genes and proteins, including peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ), CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein alpha (C/EBPα), adiponectin and fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes was significantly upregulated. Further treatment with estrogen receptor (ER) antagonist ICI 182780 and PI3K inhibitor LY 294002 revealed that BPF could promote differentiation of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes through the ER mediated phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) signaling pathway. In summary, BPF may enhance the maturation of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes by activating the ER-PI3K/AKT pathway, potentially contributing to obesity. These findings enhance the understanding of the obesogenic properties of environmental chemicals and could inform new strategies for preventing and managing obesity.

ce:abstract-sec.ce:simple-para: Bisphenols are a group of industrial chemicals widely used in the manufacture of plastics and epoxy resins. ce:section.ce:para: Bisphenol F (BPF), as one of the main alternatives to bisphenol A (BPA), is extensively utilized in epoxy resin, polycarbonate plastics, and various industrial applications (Liu et al., 2021). Given its high stability, BPF is commonly found in environmental sources like surface water, sediment, sewage discharge outlets, as well as in food and personal care items such as milk, meat, vegetables, canned foods, and grains (Chen et al., 2016; Czarny-Krzyminska et al., 2023). BPF can enter the body via dietary intake, inhalation, or dermal exposure, and its presence in human urine is comparable in frequency and concentration to that of BPA (Guo et al., 2021). A survey showed that 55 % of urine samples from residents in southern China tested positive for BPF, with a median concentration of 0.08 mg/L (Yang et al., 2014). Likewise, an American investigation found that over 60 % of adult Americans had BPF in their urine, with levels ranging from 0.15 to 0.45 μg/L (Zhou et al., 2014). These studies indicate that BPF is widely present in ecological environments and poses a high risk of human exposure. Meanwhile, the potential health hazards of BPF have been discovered gradually by researchers, such as endocrine disrupting effects, growth, and development toxicity, as well as other acute and chronic toxicity (Fatai and Aribidesi, 2022). However, the effects of BPF on obesity are currently not well defined.

Obesity, a prevalent chronic metabolic disease, has emerged as a significant health and nutrition problem worldwide, exerting a profound impact on individual well-being and public health expenditure. There are a number of consequences that are linked to obesity, including diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and malignancies (Piche et al., 2020). Preadipocytes can mature into adipocytes when conditions are favorable. Throughout this differentiation, the cells exhibit morphological changes, growing larger and adopting a rounder shape. Concurrently, abundant lipid droplets are generated within these cells. Excessive differentiation of preadipocytes into adipocytes results in significant lipid buildup within adipose tissue, a key contributor to obesity development (Zhou et al., 2021).

Obesity development is affected by multiple factors, including exposure to specific environmental pollutants, especially endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) (Amon et al., 2024). Studies have demonstrated that BPA and other EDCs are closely associated with obesity (Kahn et al., 2020). As an established environmental obesogen, BPA promotes preadipocyte differentiation via the estrogen receptor (ER) and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways (Boucher et al., 2014). With a similar chemical structure and estrogenic effects to BPA, BPF can also bind and activate ER (Shao et al., 2021). Our prior studies revealed that BPF enhances pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion in macrophages through the ER/PI3K/AKT pathway (Shi et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2021). Additionally, a link has been identified between BPF exposure and obesity among children and adolescents (Jacobson et al., 2019). Based on these findings, it is hypothesized that BPF may influence preadipocyte differentiation and contribute to obesity via ER interactions.

The mouse 3T3-L1 preadipocyte model is commonly used to study preadipocyte development and obesity. Thus, in order to investigate the effect of BPF on differentiation and its process, 3T3-L1 preadipocytes were used as an in vitro model in this study. After treating 3T3-L1 preadipocytes with different concentrations of BPF for 8 days, observe the adipogenic differentiation of the cells and explore the role of ER/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. It is hoped to provide an experimental basis for studying the potential relationship and mechanisms between BPF and obesity.

Mouse 3T3-L1 preadipocytes were cultured in DMEM, supplemented with 10 % newborn calf serum (Life Technologies, USA), 100 U/mL penicillin and streptomycin, and non-essential amino acids. The incubator conditions were maintained at 37 °C, 5 % CO2 and saturated humidity. Cells were either passaged or seeded for differentiation induction upon reaching approximately 80 % confluence. The differentiation scheme of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes is as follows (Zebisch et al., 2012). Preadipocytes were grown at a density of 8 × 104 cells per well in a 6-well plate until they reached 100 % confluence. Upon reaching confluence, cells entered a contact-inhibited state and were maintained in standard growth medium for an additional 48 h. Thereafter, differentiation medium was introduced to promote the differentiation of preadipocytes into adipocytes. During the initiation of differentiation (Day 0 - Day 2), the medium was replaced with Differentiation Medium I (DMEM + 10 % FBS + 10 μg/mL insulin +1 μM dexamethasone + 0.5 mM IBMX). Cells were incubated in this medium for 48 h. During the differentiation progression (Day 2 - Day 4), the medium was switched to Differentiation Medium II (DMEM + 10 % FBS + 10 μg/mL insulin) for another 48 h. Finally, in the maintenance stage (Day 4 - Day 8), the medium was then replaced with Differentiation Medium III (DMEM + 10 % FBS; standard maintenance medium). Cells were cultured in this medium for 4 days, allowing for full mature adipocytes.

BPF (≥98 %, Sigma-Aldrich, USA) treatment was initiated on Day 0 of 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation and continued throughout the entire differentiation period until Day 8. Cells were treated with BPF at final concentrations of 0, 5, 10 and 20 μM. To investigate the PI3K/AKT pathway or ER involvement, cells were exposed to 20 μM BPF after 1 h pre-treatment with 1 μM ER antagonist ICI 182780 (ICI) or 10 μM PI3K inhibitor LY 294002 (LY) (MedChemExpress, China). BPF and inhibitors were replenished at each medium change to maintain consistent exposure.

3T3-L1 preadipocytes were seeded at a density of 2 × 103 cells per well in a 96 well plate. Subsequently, the cells were exposed to varying concentrations of BPF (0–40 μM) for either 24 h or continuously over an 8-day period. To determine the viability of the cells, the cell counting kit-8 (Zeta Life, USA) was utilized, and the instructions provided by the manufacturer were followed.

ce:section.ce:section-title: Oil red O staining of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes
ce:section.ce:para: To assess lipid droplet formation in adipocytes, Oil Red O staining (Beyotime, Shanghai, China) was performed. After two washes with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), the cells were fixed with 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 20–30 min at room temperature. Following fixation, cells were briefly rinsed and incubated with 60 % isopropanol for 5 min to facilitate dye uptake. Subsequently, cells were stained with filtered Oil Red O working solution for 20 min. Excess stain was removed by rinsing with distilled water, and stained cells were observed and photographed under a light microscope. For quantitative analysis, the intracellular Oil Red O dye was eluted using 100 % isopropanol, and the absorbance was measured at 490 nm using a microplate reader.

A triglyceride (TG) quantification kit (JianCheng, Nanjing, China) was employed to assess intracellular TG accumulation after BPF exposure. The BCA protein assay kit (ThermoFisher Scientific USA) was used to measure the sample protein content. The following formula was used to calculate the TG content of each sample. TG content (mmol/g protein) = (absorbance of samples - absorbance of blank)/(absorbance of standard - absorbance of blank) × content of standard/protein concentration of samples.

Total RNA was extracted from 3T3-L1 cells using Trizol reagent (Takara, Japan) in accordance with standard protocols. The RNA concentration was determined with a Thermo Fisher Nanodrop, and 1 μg of RNA was subsequently reverse transcribed into cDNA using the PrimeScript™ RT Kit with gDNA Eraser (Takara, Japan). Quantitative PCR was carried out on a 96-well PikoReal Real-Time PCR System (ThermoFisher Scientific, USA) using a SYBR green kit (Takara, Japan). qRT-PCR conditions included an initial denaturation at 95 °C for 30 s, followed by 40 cycles at 95 °C for 15 s and 60 °C for 30 s. Primer sequences for PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin, FABP4, and β-actin are listed in Table 1 .

After treatment, cells were lysed in RIPA buffer supplemented with protease inhibitors. Lysates were sonicated on ice and centrifuged at 12,000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C. Protein samples were separated via SDS-PAGE and transferred onto PVDF membranes. Membranes were blocked with 5 % skim milk in TBST for 1 h and incubated overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies against PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin, FABP4, PI3K, AKT, p-PI3K, and p-AKT (Cell Signaling Technology, USA). After washing with TBST, membranes were incubated with HRP-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG for 1 h. Protein bands were detected using an enhanced chemiluminescence (ECL) detection kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA).

The results were statistically analyzed using SPSS 26.0 and visualized using GraphPad PRISM 8.0. Statistical data were presented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) and multiple groups comparisons were assessed by One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). The P value less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

ce:section.ce:section-title: BPF promoted adipogenic differentiation of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes
ce:section.ce:para: For greater clarity of the experimental procedures, the 3T3-L1 cell differentiation process and BPF treatment protocol are illustrated in a flowchart (Fig. 1 A). CCK-8 assay was conducted to evaluate the cell viability of BPF on 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, and no cytotoxicity was detected in 3T3-L1 cells after 24-h or 8-day exposure to BPF at concentrations of 0, 5, 10, 20, and 40 μM (Fig. 1B and C). Lipid droplet formation, a critical marker of preadipocyte differentiation into adipocytes, was assessed using Oil Red O staining. After 8 days of BPF treatment, lipid droplet generation in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes showed a dose-dependent increase, indicating that BPF promoted lipid droplet accumulation in these cells (Fig. 1D and F). Differentiation of preadipocytes is also marked by TG production, so intracellular TG levels were measured. Results demonstrated that TG content in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes rose with higher BPF exposure, supporting the notion that BPF enhances adipogenic differentiation (Fig. 1E).

ce:section.ce:section-title: BPF upregulated the level of adipogenic differentiation protein in 3T3-L1 cells
ce:section.ce:para: PPARγ and C/EBPα are key transcription factors in cellular lipid synthesis, crucial for regulating preadipocyte differentiation. Additionally, adiponectin and FABP4 also act as important regulators in this process. Expression of differentiation-related genes and proteins in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes was examined to corroborate the role of BPF in adipogenic differentiation. It was found that BPF could increase the expression of PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin, and FABP4 genes (Fig. 2 A–D). The results at the protein level also showed a similar situation that BPF promoted the expression of these proteins in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes (Fig. 2E–I). These data indicated that BPF may promote 3T3-L1 preadipocyte development.

ce:section.ce:section-title: PI3K/AKT pathway participated in the promotion of 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation by BPF
ce:section.ce:para: As shown in Fig. 3 A–C, the phosphorylation levels of PI3K and AKT in BPF group were significantly increased when compared with the control group, which confirmed the activating of BPF on PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. To further explore the role of PI3K/AKT pathway in BPF-induced differentiation, the PI3K-specific inhibitor, LY 294002, was applied to inhibit PI3K/AKT activation. The results revealed that co-treatment with LY 294002 and BPF significantly reduced lipid droplet formation and intracellular TG levels in 3T3-L1 cells compared to BPF treatment alone (Fig. 3D–F). These findings suggest that BPF promotes adipogenic differentiation in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes through PI3K/AKT signaling. In addition, gene and protein expression that is associated with adipogenic differentiation was evaluated following pretreatment with LY 294002 as well. The results of the investigation demonstrated that the co-treatment of LY 294002 and BPF resulted in a significant reduction in the expression of PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin, and FABP4 genes in the group that received both treatments, as compared to the group that received only BPF (Fig. 4 A–D). Similarly, the analysis of proteins demonstrated that LY 294002 was able to prevent the increase of PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin, and FABP4 protein levels that was produced by BPF (Fig. 4E–I). This study suggested that BPF may stimulate the PI3K-AKT pathway, increasing 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation.

ce:section.ce:section-title: ER participated in BPF-promoted 3T3-L1 preadipocytes differentiation
PI3K/AKT pathway mediated by ER in BPF-induced differentiation of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes
ce:section.ce:para: As a downstream pathway of ER, PI3K/AKT plays a crucial role in regulating fat development. ER can potentially suppress PPARγ production and fat formation through this signaling route. Given these findings, the ER antagonist ICI 182780 was applied to determine whether ER mediates BPF-induced activation of PI3K/AKT in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. Results indicated that PI3K and AKT phosphorylation levels were reduced in the group co-treated with ICI 182780 and BPF compared to the BPF-only group. The ability of BPF to upregulate PI3K and AKT phosphorylation was considerably diminished by the presence of ER inhibitors (Fig. 7 ). According to the findings, BPF was responsible for activating the PI3K/AKT pathway by way of the ER.

This study examined how BPF exposure influences 3T3-L1 preadipocyte differentiation and the underlying mechanisms involved. After 8 days of BPF treatment, lipid droplet accumulation and TG levels were markedly elevated in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. Key genes and proteins involved in adipogenesis, including PPARγ, C/EBPα, adiponectin, and FABP4, were significantly upregulated, indicating enhanced preadipocyte differentiation. Further studies revealed that BPF promotes differentiation through the ER-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway. Collectively, these results suggest that BPF may contribute to adipogenesis and lipid accumulation via ER/PI3K/AKT signaling, potentially linking it to obesity.

Obesity is a prevalent chronic metabolic disorder closely associated with the growth and expansion of adipose tissue (Shin et al., 2020). Adipose tissue primarily comprises adipocytes, which largely originate from preadipocyte differentiation. While genetics and lifestyle factors are key contributors, endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) like BPA have also been implicated due to their ability to disturb lipid homeostasis (Veiga-Lopez et al., 2018). BPA, recognized as an environmental obesogen, is now restricted in many countries (Boucher et al., 2014). As a BPA substitute, BPF has become widely used in consumer products. However, given its structural similarity to BPA, concerns about its metabolic impact have grown (Lee et al., 2024). Liu et al. found that BPF exposure was positively correlated with an increased risk of obesity in children and adolescents through 2013–2014 U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data (Liu et al., 2019). Jacobson et al. found that a positive correlation between BPF exposure and the incidence of abdominal obesity through 2013–2016 NHANES data (Jacobson et al., 2019). Our study aligns with these findings, demonstrating that BPF promotes lipid droplet formation and preadipocyte differentiation. These results support the notion that BPF may contribute to obesity development and underscore the need for further toxicological evaluation.

The regulation of obesity is complex, involving multiple steroid receptors, especially ER, which are prevalent in adipose tissue and play critical roles in various physiological functions (Mahboobifard et al., 2022). Recent studies have shown that some EDCs can bind to ER, producing estrogen-like effects (Ke et al., 2022; Ma et al., 2023). Many EDCs, including BPA and BPF, can bind to ER and exert estrogen-like activity, contributing to adipogenesis (Haverinen et al., 2021). Choi et al. reported that BPF induces adipogenic transcription factors even in the absence of dexamethasone (Choi et al., 2021). Ramskov et al. found that BPB, BPE, BPS and BPF affected lipid accumulation to the same extent and potencies as BPA (Ramskov Tetzlaff et al., 2020). Furthermore, Martínez et al. reported that BPF showed a greater neutral lipid storage capacity than BPA (Martinez et al., 2020). Our previous research showed that BPF could enhance macrophage pro-inflammatory factor secretion via ER-mediated signaling (Zhang et al., 2021). There have also been some studies demonstrating that BPF might have strong ER binding affinities (Karrer et al., 2018; Lei et al., 2018). Importantly, treatment with the ER antagonist ICI 182780 blocked BPF-induced early differentiation of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, further confirming the ER-dependence of this effect. These results are consistent with previous studies showing that BPF and its analogs promote adipogenesis in human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) through ER signaling (Reina-Perez et al., 2022).

The PI3K/AKT pathway plays a pivotal role in numerous physiological functions such as adipocyte differentiation, lipid synthesis, and energy homeostasis (Huang et al., 2018). AKT regulates lipid synthesis via SREBP and lipolysis via FOXO1-mediated ATGL expression (Lei et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2024). Recent studies have shown that inhibiting the PI3K/AKT pathway reduces fat accumulation and adipocyte size, promotes brown adipocyte formation, and regulates leptin, IL-6, and insulin levels (Lai et al., 2024). Li T et al. showed that pomegranate flower extract inhibited PI3K-AKT activation by reducing PI3K and p-Akt levels, thereby suppressing PPARγ expression and preadipocyte differentiation (Li et al., 2020). Our previous research has shown that BPF may disrupt insulin signaling (IRS-1/PI3K/AKT), leading to impaired glucose metabolism and altered adipokine secretion (Chen et al., 2022). These results suggested that PI3K/AKT may play a crucial role in both adipocyte lipogenesis and preadipocyte differentiation. In current study, the specific PI3K inhibitor LY294002 prevented BPF-induced differentiation of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. Additionally, we observed that BPF activated PI3K/AKT signaling via ER in these cells.

Collectively, these findings suggest that BPF may contribute to obesity through ER-mediated activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway. This study offers a new scientific foundation for understanding the promotive effect of BPF on the adipogenesis and lipogenesis of preadipocytes and provides experimental data for exploring additional physiological functions of the PI3K/AKT pathway.

In summary, this study uncovers a novel mechanism by which BPF enhances differentiation and adipogenesis of 3T3-L1 preadipocytes via the ER-mediated PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. These findings suggest that BPF may contribute to the development of obesity by promoting adipocyte maturation, underscoring its role as a potential obesogenic factor. Essentially, this study provides valuable insights into the complex relationship between BPF and obesity, enhancing the understanding of the potential mechanisms driving obesity progression. Aside from that, these findings may pave the way for identifying new therapeutic targets and provide promising avenues for preventing and treating this common health condition.
